reason: The text depicts Pharaoh's government and leadership as a negative model that fails to benefit the people. Throughout the passage, Pharaoh refuses to heed warnings and allow the Hebrew people to leave, despite the plagues devastating Egypt and causing immense suffering to the Egyptian population. The text explicitly shows that Egypt is destroyed ('אָבְדָה מִצְרָיִם' - 'Egypt is destroyed') and the people suffer from plague after plague: water turning to blood (eliminating their water supply), frogs, locusts destroying vegetation, darkness, and ultimately the death of the firstborn. Pharaoh's government remains non-functional and harmful to his own people, as he stubbornly refuses to change course ('וַיְחַזֵּק לֵב פַּרְעֹה' - 'Pharaoh's heart was hardened') even when it becomes clear his leadership is bringing national disaster. The passage presents an exemplar of failed, destructive leadership that disregards the welfare of the people.
